name: form
title: Form
description: One set of fields a player fills in and sends together. It does not submit: it cancels the browser's own submission, reads what the player typed out of the fields and hands it to the host as `{ fieldName: value }`, and the host does the network call, the validation and the decision about what happens next. Errors come back from the host as sentences, render as a summary above the fields and are counted on `data-gs-error-count`, so a test reads the number without parsing the prose. `busy` is the window between the player pressing send and the host answering: it is host-declared, it rides `data-gs-busy` and `aria-busy`, and the form says so in words rather than sitting unchanged, which is the dead end the spec forbids.
docs: Pass `name` and `label`, put `field` components in the children and the submit control in `actions`. `onSubmit` gives you `(values, event)` where `values` is what the player typed, keyed by each field's `name`; an unticked checkbox is absent, exactly as it is in a native submission. Set `busy` while your own call is in flight and clear it when you answer, and pass `errors` as `[{ field, reason }]` when you reject values. Find the summary with `[data-gs-part="summary"]` and the count with `[data-gs-error-count]`.
